intl.title: Tarleton State - International applicants (requirements, English proficiency, deadlines)

gs.title: Tarleton State - President's Guaranteed Scholarship Program (freshman)

test_policy.notes: SAT/ACT/CLT scores are not required for an admission decision; they are encouraged for scholarships or to fulfil the TSI requirement. First-time freshmen from a foreign high school are exempt from the Texas Uniform Admissions Policy and are reviewed individually (including GPA); scores can help individual review. Students at a U.S. high school on a visa follow the Texas public/private/out-of-state rank-and-curriculum rules.

requirements.notes: Online application, $50 non-refundable fee, official domestic transcript or an international transcript evaluation (NACES/AICE member, in English, must include GPA and GPA scale), proof of English proficiency. After admission: affidavit of financial support, bank letter or statement, and passport copy. Allow at least 60 days for document processing. Recommendation letters are not required but accepted.

deadlines.label: International fall application deadline (fall 2027 entry)
deadlines.notes: Enforced international deadlines: Spring Nov. 1, Summer Mar. 15 (generally not accepted for undergraduates except Medical Laboratory Science majors), Fall June 15. Years are not printed; fall 2027 assumed. Domestic freshmen: fall Aug. 1 (the Common Data Set also lists a Mar. 1 priority date).

deadlines.label: General scholarship application priority date (fall 2027 entry)
deadlines.notes: President's Guaranteed Scholarship Program: applying through the Tarleton General Scholarship application is required; later applications are considered as funding allows. The page does not state whether international students are eligible.

english_policy.waiver_notes: Exempt: citizens of listed English-speaking countries (e.g. Australia, Canada except Quebec, Ireland, Jamaica, Ghana, Nigeria, New Zealand, United Kingdom); 6 college hours of English incl. 3 of composition (C or better) at a U.S., Canadian (non-Quebec), British or Australian institution; SAT EBRW 550 or ACT English 21; two years at an accredited U.S. high school; a school letter confirming all secondary education was in English (reviewed by Admissions); or completion of Level 9 at The Language Company. Scores must be no more than 2 years old at the start of the term (TOEFL/IELTS valid 3 years, PTE/Duolingo 2 years per the footnote).

english.notes: Internet-based TOEFL. The page also accepts TOEFL Essentials 7 and TOEFL ITP Plus for China 460.
Listed as '69 or 3.5 (effective 1/21/2026)'; the page does not name the 1-6 scale.

aid.notes: The President's Guaranteed Scholarship (first-time freshmen in the top half of their high school class) pays $500 to $4,000 a year depending on rank and test scores, renewable up to 4 years; only students in the top 25% may qualify for an out-of-state tuition waiver. The page does not say whether international students are eligible, and no international-specific scholarship is published, so aid policy is left unset.
